question: For pretraining a small 100M-parameter code LLM, what is the smallest practical mix of bigcode/the-stack-v2 (or the-stack-smol) python data and starcoderdata that yields a useful dataset under ~3 GB raw download on disk? Include dedup, license filtering, rows-per-token estimates, and best streaming approach.
answer:
To pretrain a 100M-parameter model under a 3GB limit, use the-stack-smol, which provides a high-quality, pre-filtered subset of 30 languages, including Python [1]. It is specifically sized at ~2.6GB of text, fitting your constraint perfectly [1].

For loading, use Hugging Face streaming to avoid local storage overhead [2][1]:

```python
from datasets import load_dataset
# Streaming Python subset specifically
ds = load_dataset("bigcode/the-stack-smol", data_dir="data/python", streaming=True)
```

The-stack-smol includes near-deduplication and license filtering (permissive/no-license) via the BigCode pipeline [2][1]. For row-to-token estimates, note that the 300,000 total rows in the-stack-smol represent 0.1% of the original dataset, useful for rapid prototyping [1]. If you require larger volumes, switch to streaming the-stack-v2-train-smol-ids, but note that it requires specific SWH access credentials to fetch file contents [2][3]. Use the basic, stars, and fertility filters if you perform custom preprocessing on raw code [4].
